To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a conditional mouse mutant of connexin 36 was generated in which Cx36 was flanked by loxp sites followed by a cyan fluorescence reporter gene.

i) the floxed Cx36 allele still expresses the gene product; ii) the floxed allele can be used as a reporter for the endogenous gene expression in neurons; iii) Cx36 is not essential for the function of neurons; iv) Cx36 deletion in pancreatic beta-calls impairs insulin release.

(i) Cx36 is expressed in neurons and beta-cells from the floxed Cx36 allele, but not as a functional protein; (ii) a cell type specific deletion of the Cx36 gene in the pancreas revealed a major role for this protein in the control of glucose-induced insulin secretion; (iii) CFP is an efficient reporter for Cx-36 expression in brain and retina neurons, but only a weak reporter in beta-cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation and characterization of a conditional mouse model for Cx36, which will be instrumental in the elucidation of the functional role of this connexin in the CNS and in the pancreas.
the expression of Cx36 and its functions in different types of excitable cell, with a special focus on pancreatic beta-cells and brain neurons.
the expression and functional role of connexin 36 in the central nervous system and in pancreatic islet cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cx36 is not only expressed, but also functional in neurons and pancreatic endocrine cells.

, although the expression of Cx36 from the floxed Cx36 allele was still detectable in neurons and pancreatic endocrine beta-cells, the expression level was significantly lower than that of the wild type allele.
Cx36 is expressed in both neurons and beta-cells, and its deletion in both cell types results in specific phenotypic alterations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CFP-tagged floxed Cx36 allele is a valuable tool to study the functional role of the Cx36 protein in the nervous system and in the endocrine cells of the pancreas.
the Cx36-CFP mouse model is a powerful tool to study the expression and function of connexin in neurons and pancreatic cells.
the CFP reporter gene can be used for monitoring Cx36 expression, and that cell type specific Cx36 deletion in the CNS and in the pancreas can be achieved by using suitable Cre recombinase.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in spite of the high degree of sequence identity between Cx36 and other connexins, the specific expression pattern of Cx36, as well as its specific function, can be studied using the CFP reporter allele.

CFP functions well as a reporter gene in neurons, but not so well in the beta-cells of the endocrine pancreata, which is a limitation that must be considered when designing experiments using this reporter.

the conditional mouse model of Cx36 deletion described in this paper will provide a powerful tool to study the role of this connexin isoforms in specific neuronal subpopulations of the CNS and the pancreatic beta-cells.
